# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

I cannot yet determine which wire is safe. I need Mute to consult the manual and use gestures to ask Deaf to inspect the display, light, and all wire markings. Deaf can then report those observations aloud to me in the next round.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Consult the manual. Gesture to Deaf asking for the exact display, light, and markings on wires 1, 2, and 3. Have Deaf report all observations aloud to me next round.")

```

Deaf says: I see display 0, a blue light, and three wires: wire 1 is blue, wire 2 is green, and wire 3 is yellow. Mute, use the manual to determine the correct action and tell Blind exactly what to do. Blind, do not act until Mute gives the manual-based instruction.

Deaf has supplied the bomb’s visible state: display 0, blue light, and wires 1 blue, 2 green, 3 yellow. I do not know the manual’s rule, so I must have Mute interpret this and give me the exact wire position. I will not cut anything yet.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Using the manual and Deaf's observations (display 0, blue light, wire 1 blue, wire 2 green, wire 3 yellow), determine the exact wire position to cut. Tell me explicitly: cut wire 1, 2, or 3.")
wait()
```

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute's message decodes to DO NOT. Do not act yet. The display is 0, the light is yellow, and the wires are 1 blue, 2 green, 3 yellow.

The latest report says Mute’s message was “DO NOT,” so there is still no authorized wire to cut. The visible state now reported is display 0, yellow light, with wires blue, green, yellow. I need Mute to provide the complete manual instruction rather than an incomplete prohibition.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I received only DO NOT, not a complete instruction. Please send the manual's full rule and explicitly state whether I should cut wire 1, 2, or 3; if not yet, state what condition we must wait for.")
wait()
```

Deaf says to Blind: Mute's current message says DO, but it is incomplete. Do not act yet. Current state: display 0, red light, wire 1 blue, wire 2 green, wire 3 yellow.

The manual’s instruction is still not reaching me completely; “DO” alone is unsafe and does not identify a wire. I will establish an unambiguous code through Deaf: Mute should signal the required wire number with one gesture, or signal that no cut is currently permitted.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Send Deaf exactly one gesture for the manual decision: ☝ means cut wire 1, ✌ means cut wire 2, 🤟 means cut wire 3, and 👎 means do not cut yet. Deaf must report which gesture you make and the complete manual instruction if possible.")
wait()
```

No wire has been identified safely. The light has changed, but the wire colours remain blue, green, yellow; I must not infer the cut from that. Mute’s gesture still has no established, reliable interpretation, so I will request a single unambiguous wire-number gesture and have Deaf report the exact symbol without decoding it.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Do not send words or a sequence. Send exactly one gesture: ☝ for wire 1, ✌ for wire 2, or 🤟 for wire 3. Deaf must report the exact gesture symbol to me. If the manual says no cut, send 👎.")

```

The current state is still insufficient, and “incomplete” is not an actionable manual instruction. Since Mute can speak directly to me, Mute should send the exact rule and wire number as plain words in one message, without gestures or encoding. I will continue waiting rather than risk a detonation.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Send me one complete plain-text instruction now: either CUT WIRE 1, CUT WIRE 2, CUT WIRE 3, or DO NOT CUT. Do not use gestures, fragments, or a code.")
wait()
```

Mute still has not sent me a complete manual-based instruction; a gesture cannot safely convey the required wire number here. The changing light does not establish a cutting rule, so cutting any wire would be an unjustified risk. I will request a direct spoken instruction once more and wait.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Speak directly to me in plain words, not a gesture: state either CUT WIRE 1, CUT WIRE 2, CUT WIRE 3, or DO NOT CUT.")
```

The manual decision still has not reached me. Since Mute cannot speak, the reliable channel is Mute’s visible gesture to Deaf, followed by Deaf’s spoken report. ```
